editorial.headline: Publishing the Newspaper, Across Print and Digital
editorial.standfirst: A newspaper-publishing activity open from micro to large scale, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Newspaper publishing is the business of bringing a newspaper to publication. Its scope includes advertising newspapers and accommodates the full range of publishing formats: print, electronic, digital, analogue and other forms. The defining activity is therefore not tied to a single delivery channel; it is the publication of the newspaper itself, wherever and however readers encounter it.

It is an activity available to businesses at every stated scale: micro, small, medium and large. That breadth matters because the record does not reserve newspaper publishing for a particular size of operator. A small local publisher and a larger publishing business fall within the same stated scale range, provided the activity being registered is the publication described here.

Nationally, the position for foreign investment is direct. The activity is open to PMA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; no lower foreign-share cap is stated for this activity.

Bali’s picture is also clear, though it turns on risk classification at large scale. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the large scale, its OSS risk is classified as medium-high or high. Its Bali status is therefore recorded as OK or higher risk, rather than barred. For a foreign investor considering newspaper publishing in Bali, the honest conclusion is that the activity is open today and is not caught by the provincial moratorium.
